object_entity.notes: First ecumenical council convened by Emperor Constantine at Nicaea in Bithynia, May–August 325 CE. Addressed the Arian controversy; produced the original Nicene Creed affirming the Son as homoousios (same substance) with the Father; condemned Arius; standardized Easter dating; addressed the Meletian schism in Egypt. Attended by ~300 bishops, mostly from the East. Jacob of Nisibis and Eusebius of Caesarea were among the attendees.

evidence.notes: Eusebius of Caesarea attended and wrote an account of Nicaea in his letter to his church (apud Theodoret HE 1.11) and in Vita Constantini 3.

passage.excerpt: Constantine convened the universal synod at Nicaea in Bithynia, gathering bishops from all regions of the empire.
